sources.title: Towards a Papuan history of languages
sources.note: Linguistic analysis explaining that Papuan languages comprise separate families and cannot be treated as one genealogical or social unit.

sources.title: Language as a lens into the prehistory of West New Guinea
sources.note: ANU synthesis documenting more than 260 languages, roughly thirty families, and eighteen isolates in western New Guinea.

sources.title: Forty Years in the South Seas
sources.note: Open archaeological volume surveying more than fifty thousand years of New Guinea and western Pacific history and later Austronesian interaction.

sources.title: Kuk Early Agricultural Site
sources.note: UNESCO evidence for long-lived wetland management, independent agriculture, bananas, taro, yam, mounds, and drainage ditches.

sources.title: Reading Early Agriculture at Kuk Swamp
sources.note: Peer-reviewed report presenting competing interpretations and dates rather than hiding scholarly disagreement about early cultivation.

sources.title: Emergence of a Neolithic in highland New Guinea
sources.note: Peer-reviewed Waim excavations on early fiber craft, pestles, figurative stone, axes, obsidian movement, and independent highland innovation.

sources.title: The Archaeology of Southern New Guinea
sources.note: Academic regional synthesis of pottery, settlement, trade, exchange, and cultural interaction on the southern Papuan coast.

sources.title: Petrographic analyses of Kikiniu ceramics
sources.note: Peer-reviewed ceramic study identifying Gulf pottery around 1550 to 1000 calibrated years BP and probable sago-linked exchange.

sources.title: Origin of sweet potato genetic diversity in New Guinea
sources.note: Peer-reviewed genetic and historical synthesis on disputed introductions, likely post-1500 movement, and rapid highland adoption around 1700.

sources.title: Ancient and historic dispersals of sweet potato in Oceania
sources.note: Peer-reviewed commentary connecting New Guinea lineages mainly with post-European dispersal while retaining uncertainty and earlier taro agriculture.

sources.title: Ten Thousand Years of Cultivation at Kuk Swamp
sources.note: ANU archaeological chapter on later Kuk cultivation, sweet potato, shell and axe movement, and braided local trade routes.

sources.title: Cultural Landscapes of the Pacific
sources.note: UNESCO thematic study on Kuk, sweet potato, pigs, marriage and compensation exchanges, and non-teleological histories of agriculture.

sources.title: Frontier Archaeology in the Lower Tagali Valley
sources.note: Open peer-reviewed excavation of early nineteenth-century Huli houses, gardens, drains, gendered space, pigs, and oral-genealogical chronology.

sources.title: Bioarchaeological analysis of south-coast New Guinea health
sources.note: Papua New Guinea Medical Journal abstract comparing teeth and childhood stress at late prehistoric Nebira and Motupore.

sources.title: Prehistoric migration at Nebira
sources.note: Peer-reviewed isotope and burial study showing mobility, differentiated graves, and interpretive limits at one south-coast community.

sources.title: Archaeology of Lapita Dispersal in Oceania
sources.note: ANU archaeological evidence for long-lived settlements, house posts, reused burials, and dog-tooth ornaments at Nebira and neighboring sites.

sources.title: Origin and development of Motupore village
sources.note: University-linked archaeological project on Motupore settlement chronology and its relationship to southern coastal exchange.

sources.title: Arts of Oceania
sources.note: Museum synthesis on regional exchange, kula partnerships, canoe voyaging, pearl shell, Sepik painting, ancestors, and initiation.

sources.title: Learning Process: Stone tools in the Highlands
sources.note: Australian Museum account of observed highland stone-tool knowledge, manufacture, teaching, and varied work in organic materials.

sources.title: Geochemistry and sources of stone tools in south-west New Britain
sources.note: Museum-published geochemical study tracing flaked, dressed, and ground tools through intra-island and inter-island exchange.

sources.title: Stone mortar and pestle distribution in New Britain
sources.note: Museum-published archaeological study cautiously connecting dated mortars and pestles with ancient taro cultivation.

sources.title: Nineteenth-century New Guinea outrigger canoe model
sources.note: Museum object record for a carved, pigmented southeast New Guinea outrigger model acquired before 1887.

sources.title: Elema mask from New Guinea
sources.note: Museum record linking an Elema barkcloth mask to Samuel Macfarlane correspondence and collections present by the 1870s.

sources.title: Narrative of the Voyage of HMS Rattlesnake, volume two
sources.note: Public-domain 1852 primary publication with a Redscar Bay vocabulary collected during the 1846 to 1850 survey.

sources.title: Papua New Guinea Department of Foreign Affairs history
sources.note: Official overview of early European encounters, the nominal Dutch claim of 1828, Moresby surveys, and later partitions.

sources.title: Oceanic Negroes: British anthropology of Papuans, 1820 to 1869
sources.note: ANU history of the racialized European category Papuan, its earlier usages, and changing descriptions after first encounters.

sources.title: Malay Knowledge, Spanish Voyages, and Indigenous Presence
sources.note: Peer-reviewed reconstruction of the 1545 Ortiz de Retes voyage, Indigenous presence, Malay knowledge, place names, and mapping.

sources.title: An Archaeological Review of Western New Guinea
sources.note: Peer-reviewed regional synthesis of fragmentary archaeology, long interaction with Island Southeast Asia, trade, and early recorded encounters.

sources.title: Early modern slave trade prices in the Indian Ocean and Indonesian Archipelago
sources.note: Peer-reviewed comparative history documenting Papuan captives in eastern Indonesian slave gifting and trade without making the system island-wide.

sources.title: Samuel Macfarlane
sources.note: Australian Dictionary of Biography chronology for 1871 reconnaissance, 1874 return, village visits, mission stations, languages, and controversy.

sources.title: History of Research in Austronesian Languages of Southeast Papua
sources.note: ANU linguistic historiography dating Redscar Bay wordlists to 1849 and distinguishing Motu from neighboring languages and later grammars.

sources.title: Murray 1876 language-documentation record
sources.note: Glottolog bibliographic classification of Murray’s 1876 book as ethnography and wordlist covering several distinct regional languages.

sources.title: Indigenous Intermediaries
sources.note: ANU Press history centering Indigenous brokers, translators, guides, and knowledge in exploration archives rather than treating voyagers as solitary discoverers.

sources.title: Papuan Pasts
sources.note: ANU research volume integrating cultural, linguistic, archaeological, and biological histories while preserving the plurality of Papuan-speaking peoples.

sources.title: Papua New Guinea: colonial partition
sources.note: National Museum of Australia account of the 1884 German annexation and British protectorate following earlier Dutch claims.
